Synopsis:
Shadowheart reacts to taking offerings made at a shrine to Selûne, the rival of her goddess Shar. If Shadowheart is the avatar, she has a moment of introspection where she considers if she should take the items of not. If Shadowheart is a companion, she encourages the player to not take the items. The player can try talk her around, and may discover she is a Shar worshipper if they don't already know. The outcome of this dialogue potentially strengthens or damages Shadowheart's opinion of the player.

retrieved_synopses: Shadowheart reacts to taking offerings made at a shrine to Selûne, the rival of her goddess Shar. If Shadowheart is the avatar, she has a moment of introspection where she considers if she should take the items of not. If Shadowheart is a companion, she encourages the player to not take the items. The player can try talk her around, and may discover she is a Shar worshipper if they don't already know. The outcome of this dialogue potentially strengthens or damages Shadowheart's opinion of the player.

Shadowheart comments upon a statue of Selûne, located somewhat incongruously in a camp full of goblin marauders. Shadowheart is a little perturbed by the statue's presence, but quickly dismissive of it. Selûne is a rival to her own goddess; the statue deserves an ignominious fate. If Shadowheart is not know to be a Shar worshipper, she's a little more reserved in her comments.

Venturing farther into what is now a goblin camp but was once a temple of Selûne (the moon goddess, rival to her own goddess, Shar), Shadowheart reacts with disgust. She notes how the crude goblin decoration is an improvement upon the surviving signs of Selûne worship. If Shadowheart isn't known to be a Shar worshipper, her comments are a little more veiled.

Shadowheart pauses and reflects to herself after entering the main chamber of what was once an impressive temple dedicated to the moon goddess, Selune. Being a worshipper of Selune's rival, Shar, Shadowheart is satisfied to see the temple ruined and full of goblins, but also is curious as to what happened. She may suspect that fellow Sharrans were active in the region at some point in the past, and may have been responsible for the temple's desecration.

On approaching an ancient mural in the goblin camp, Shadowheart recognises it was once decorated to honour the moon goddess. Selûne. A worshipper of Selûne's rival, Shar, Shadowheart reacts with distaste and ill ease (if Shadowheart hasn't revealed her true nature yet, her observations are a little more veiled.)
context: The party has come across offerings at a shrine to Selûne tucked in a ruined temple/goblin camp; the items are presented as possible loot but are explicitly tied to Selûne worship. Shadowheart is a follower of Shar, Selûne’s rival: if she’s a companion she urges the player to leave or even destroy the offerings and warns they could be cursed, while if she is the avatar she has a private moment of doubt about taking them. The player can try to persuade her, take the items anyway, or even probe thoughts (there are lines where the player suggests using a parasite/mind‑reach), which can force Shadowheart to reveal more or lash out. How the player handles this can uncover her faith (if not already known) and will change Shadowheart’s opinion of them.
